To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the flavor democracy and mass degeneracy hypotheses are consistent with current neutrino oscillation data and 2) a large mixing and CP violation in the neutrino sector is predicted.

(1) the flavor democracy of the charged leptons and mass degeneracy (or near degeneracy) of the neutrinos lead to a large mixing angle in neutrino oscillation; (2) the large mixing angle can explain the atmospheric and solar neutrinos; (3) the CP or T violation in neutrino mixing is small but measurable; (4) the similarity and difference between the flavor mixing of leptons and quarks are understood in a unified framework; and (5)
the flavor democracy of leptons leads naturally to the large mixing and CP violation of neutrinos and that the flavor democracy can be realized in nature by a simple symmetry principle.
